stories.title: Plans Filed for 155-Unit Office-to-Apartment Conversion in Boston
stories.excerpt: Boston continues to be a hub for office conversion enthusiasts, with Kendall Capital planning to convert a landmark office building in Boston’s Financial District into a 155-unit residential property. The 155,000-square-foot project would be financed through historic tax credits, according to a report by Banker & Tradesman. Kendall Capital manager Mai Luo acquired the property from B.E. Realist LP for $15.75 million last December, public records show. Located at 133 Federal St., the 12-story Brutalist building formerly known as the Blue Cross-Blue Shield Building was built in 1960 and certified as a landmark by the city in 2024. The redevelopment project is anticipated to take 16 to 24 months and would create a mix of apartments including 118 studios with rents ranging from $2,500 to $4,500. An application submitted to the Boston Planning Department states that all of the current leases are subject to owner termination rights in the next 18 months. The post Plans Filed for 155-Unit Office-to-Apartment Conversion in Boston appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Kendall Capital converting 155-unit office tower at 133 Federal St., Boston Financial District.
118 studios priced $2,500–$4,500/month; 16–24 month timeline using historic tax credits.
All current office leases subject to termination within 18 months; acquisition price $15.75M.
stories.summary: Kendall Capital is converting the landmark 1960 Blue Cross-Blue Shield Building (155,000 sf) into 155 apartments, predominantly studios, financed via historic tax credits. The deal capitalizes on the building's 2024 landmark designation and upcoming lease expirations. Studio rents range from $2,500 to $4,500/month, and construction is estimated at 16–24 months.
stories.impact: Boston's office-to-residential conversion wave continues to signal structural office oversupply and strong rental demand for studio/flex units in downtown submarkets. Developers should monitor lease expiration cycles in other landmark Boston office buildings as near-term conversion windows; historic tax credits remain critical to financial feasibility. This activity suggests limited new-build upside in the CBD and points demand toward flex/adaptive-use plays.

stories.title: Growing Biotech Firm Leases 33K SF in New Haven
stories.excerpt: Biotech firm Invivyd is more than tripling its headquarters space in downtown New Haven, CT by signing a long-term lease for about 33,000 square feet at a landmark building neighboring Yale University. The transaction was reported by Hartford Business Journal. Invivyd will take space at 205 Church St., an historic building originally constructed in 1832 and renovated in 2015. The building sits next door to Invivyd’s current 9,000-square-foot headquarters at 209 Church St. The new premises include 17,322 square feet of ground-floor space, 12,563 square feet on the mezzanine and 2,750 square feet in the basement. Savills worked on behalf of Invivyd in the transaction, while CBRE represented the building owner, Cooper Church LLC, which is controlled by investor David Kuperberg, according to state business records. Invivyd develops treatments for infectious diseases and was formerly based in Waltham, MA, where the company maintains a research and development lab. The post Growing Biotech Firm Leases 33K SF in New Haven appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Invivyd expanding HQ from 9,000 sf to 42,000 sf at 205 Church St., New Haven.
Company moving from Waltham, MA; retaining R&D lab; headquarters consolidation signals biotech cluster growth.
Yale-adjacent location with historic building; long-term lease indicates commitment to market.
stories.summary: Invivyd, an infectious disease biotech firm, is tripling its New Haven headquarters footprint to 42,000 sf in a renovated 1832 building adjacent to its current 9,000 sf space. The company is relocating its main operations from Waltham while maintaining R&D in Massachusetts. The move signals confidence in New Haven's biotech ecosystem and proximity to Yale University.
stories.impact: Biotech/life sciences expansion in New Haven will drive near-term office absorption and could catalyze multifamily demand if Invivyd adds headcount and attracts talent migration from Boston/Waltham. Developers should monitor Yale innovation corridor for satellite residential demand; mixed-income, transit-oriented apartments near Church Street corridor could capture high-skill workforce inflow. This is an early signal of secondary biotech hub formation.

stories.title: Podcast: Automating CRE Accounts Payable Coding, with PredictAP CEO David Stifter
stories.excerpt: David Stifter has spent more than two decades at the intersection of real estate, technology, and finance. As Managing Director and functional CTO at Digital Bridge (formerly Colony Capital), he led data architecture, process improvement, and finance transformation initiatives across major acquisitions. In 2020, he co-founded PredictAP with a team of B2B SaaS and AI veterans from Blizzard, Apple, and HubSpot. Since then, the company has grown to serve more than 130 real estate firms and process more than 7 million invoices a year. David is based in Lincoln, MA. (02:20) From Colony Capital to founding PredictAP (05:11) When a $60B firm couldn’t pay bills (07:23) Why invoice coding is harder than it looks (09:29) CAM pools, triple net leases, and the permutation problem (13:43) When institutional knowledge walks out the door (16:38) How to tell a real solution from a pretty demo (20:48) PredictAP: From inbox to Yardi in 30 seconds (24:47) Related Group, Cushman & Wakefield, and what 130 clients taught PredictAP (27:59) Why integration makes or breaks AP automation (30:17) Build vs. buy: what CFOs & COOs get wrong (33:51) Sheriff vs. shepherd: how to manage AI adoption internally (35:50) AP coding, audit risk, and financial misstatement (38:44) Collaboration superpower: Richard Feynman Learn more: –Visit PredictAP –David Stifter on LinkedIn Virtual Events: –AI & Innovation Forum: Multifamily: on 9/29 –Spotlight Case Study: Inside the AI Transformation at Cushman & Wakefield: on 10/8 In-person Events: –Institutional Investors & PE Forum: in NYC on 9/16 –South Florida Capital & Development Forum: in Miami on 10/15 –Finance Forum: in NYC on 11/3 –All upcoming Commercial Observer events Connect with Tangent: -Edward Cohen on LinkedIn -Zach Aarons on LinkedIn -Tangent on LinkedIn
bullets: PredictAP CEO David Stifter discusses AP automation software for real estate firms.
Company serves 130+ RE clients, processes 7M invoices/year; founded 2020 by B2B/AI veterans.
Podcast focuses on invoice coding, CAM pools, integration with property management systems.
stories.summary: Podcast episode featuring PredictAP CEO David Stifter on accounts payable automation for real estate. The company serves over 130 real estate firms and processes 7 million invoices annually. Topics include invoice coding, triple-net lease complexity, and integration with platforms like Yardi.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development strategy, supply, demand, or capital availability. This is an operational/back-office software story, not a market signal.

stories.title: Long Island City Commercial Building Changes Hands for $6M
stories.excerpt: A local developer has purchased a commercial unit in Long Island City for $6.1 million, or approximately $407 per buildable square foot, with plans to redevelop the building into high-end condos. Marcus & Millichap negotiated the sale of the now-vacant property at 49-03 Fifth St., which was formerly home to an auto repair shop. The brokerage’s Sean Fopeano, Shaun Riney and David Cornejo exclusively marketed the property on behalf of the private family seller and procured the buyer. The property sits on a 0.11-acre lot and features 10,000 s/f of unused air rights. The asset is located within an M1-4/R6A zoning district, which offers mixed-use redevelopment opportunities, about one block from the LIC waterfront and one block from Vernon Boulevard. Gantry Plaza State Park, I-495, and the Long Island City Train Station are situated nearby. Fopeano noted that the buyer is planning a boutique condominium development with over 30 high-end units and is underwriting sellout pricing north of $1,600 per square foot. Image courtesy of Marcus & Millichap. The post Long Island City Commercial Building Changes Hands for $6M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Local developer acquires vacant auto-repair property at 49-03 Fifth St., Long Island City for $6.1M.
Asset priced $407/sf buildable; includes 10,000 sf air rights; zoned M1-4/R6A mixed-use.
Buyer underwriting 30+ high-end condo units at $1,600+/sf sellout pricing; one block from LIC waterfront.
stories.summary: A Long Island City mixed-use property sold for $6.1 million ($407/sf buildable), with the buyer planning a boutique 30+ unit condo development at $1,600+/sf. The 0.11-acre lot includes 10,000 sf of air rights and sits in an M1-4/R6A zone, one block from the waterfront. Marcus & Millichap brokered the transaction.
stories.impact: LIC waterfront-adjacent sites continue to trade at aggressive pricing and attract condo rather than rental development, reflecting tight supply and high land values in trophy submarkets. However, the $1,600+/sf condo pricing assumptions are narrow and cap-rate-sensitive; rising rates or absorption headwinds could stress underwriting. For rental developers, this signals that LIC conversion/redevelopment economics are tightening and that supply-constrained submarkets may favor rental-to-condo transitions rather than new MF builds.

stories.title: Marcus & Millichap Arranges Sale of 206-Unit Indiana MF Property
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap announced the sale of Shoaff Park Villas, a 206-unit multifamily property in Fort Wayne, Indiana. “Shoaff Park Villas presented a rare opportunity as it was the first time the property had been offered for sale since 1976 after being owned by the same family for 50 years,” said Jack Friskney, director of investments. “The buyer plans to complete larger-scale interior renovations, positioning the property to capture future rental growth in a market supported by steady population gains and long-term affordability.” Friskney, Aaron Kuroiwa and Austin Meeker, investment specialists in Marcus & Millichap’s Indianapolis office, had the exclusive listing to market the property on behalf of the seller, Shoaff Park Villas Apartments Inc. and procured the buyer, an Illinois-based investor with a regional portfolio in northern Indiana and southern Michigan. Located at 4604 Jason Drive, Shoaff Park Villas consists of 24 studio apartments, 130 one-bedroom, one-bath units and 52 two-bedroom, one-bath units. The post Marcus & Millichap Arranges Sale of 206-Unit Indiana MF Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shoaff Park Villas, 206-unit property, Fort Wayne, Indiana sold after 50 years under same ownership.
Unit mix: 24 studios, 130 one-bed, 52 two-bed; buyer planning larger-scale interior renovations.
Illinois-based investor with regional northern Indiana/southern Michigan portfolio; market supported by population gains and affordability.
stories.summary: Shoaff Park Villas, a 206-unit Fort Wayne, Indiana multifamily property held by the same family since 1976, sold to an Illinois-based investor with a regional portfolio. The buyer plans interior renovations to capture future rental growth in a market noted for steady population gains and long-term affordability. Marcus & Millichap facilitated the transaction.
stories.impact: Fort Wayne multifamily is attracting outside capital and value-add operators, signaling flight-to-quality in secondary markets where supply is limited and demographic/migration tailwinds persist. The 50-year hold by a single family owner suggests limited property-level capital reinvestment; new ownership and renovation cycles may tighten supply and drive rent growth. Developers should monitor Fort Wayne's population trends and employment base to identify future new-build windows, especially in workforce housing.

stories.title: Becovic Residential Acquires Historic Andersonville Property
stories.excerpt: Becovic Residential has acquired the historic mixed-use property at 5154 N. Clark Street for $20 million and is introducing it under its new name, The Quarters at Andersonville. Built in 1923 and occupying a full city block at the intersection of Clark Street, Foster Avenue and Ashland Avenue, The Quarters at Andersonville includes 81 apartments and 10 ground-floor commercial spaces. The property had been held by its previous owner for more than 40 years. The acquisition marks Becovic Residential’s entry into Andersonville and extends the company’s presence across Chicago’s North Side. Becovic Management Group, Inc. will provide property management services for the property. Essex Realty Group served as broker for the transaction. Financing was provided by Associated Bank, with Elizabeth Hozian handling the financing relationship. “The Quarters at Andersonville is a special addition to Becovic,” said Sal Becovic, President of Becovic Residential. “We see our role as caring for this property and being a good neighbor to the community around it. Andersonville is a natural extension of our presence across the North Side.” The post Becovic Residential Acquires Historic Andersonville Property appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Becovic Residential acquires The Quarters at Andersonville, 81-unit historic mixed-use property for $20M.
Built 1923, full city block at Clark/Foster/Ashland; includes 10 ground-floor retail spaces; held 40+ years.
Becovic extends North Side presence; Associated Bank financing; marks company's entry into Andersonville submarket.
stories.summary: Becovic Residential acquired a historic mixed-use property at 5154 N. Clark Street in Chicago's Andersonville neighborhood for $20 million. The 1923 building encompasses 81 apartments and 10 ground-floor commercial spaces on a full city block. This marks Becovic's entry into Andersonville and expands its North Side multifamily footprint.
stories.impact: Becovic's move into Andersonville signals expanding operator interest in established, transit-accessible Chicago North Side neighborhoods with stable demographics and limited new supply. The 81-unit count is modest but the ground-floor retail component offers upside optionality. Developers should assess Andersonville's zoning and entitlement capacity for future infill/adaptive-use plays; limited new supply and North Side gentrification momentum suggest strong absorption fundamentals for mid-rise rental projects in transit corridors.

stories.title: Private Equity Firm Sentinel Capital Expands to 35K SF at One Vanderbilt
stories.excerpt: Private equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners has expanded to 34,737 square feet at One Vanderbilt. The deal gives Sentinel an additional 7,134 square feet of office space on a portion of the tower’s 54th floor, according to a Monday announcement by landlord SL Green Realty. The move brings Sentinel’s total footprint at the trophy high-rise to 34,737 square feet. The lease term and asking rent for the expansion were not disclosed, but SL Green’s Steven Durels told Commercial Observer in February that rents in the building ranged from $250 to “well over $300” per square foot. In-house brokers represented SL Green in the transaction, while Newmark’s Brian Waterman and David Waterman negotiated on behalf of Sentinel Capital. The 1.7 million-square-foot tower, located at 1 Vanderbilt Avenue just west of Grand Central Terminal, remains 100 percent leased, according to SL Green. Law firm Greenberg Traurig recently signed a 10.5-year deal for another 33,477 square feet at the high-rise, CO reported this month, bringing its total footprint to 133,365 square feet. Other office tenants at One Vanderbilt include TD Bank, investment management firm Carlyle Group, alternative investment firm Oak Hill Advisors and SL Green itself. Spokespeople for Sentinel Capital and Newmark did not respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Sentinel Capital Partners expands to 34,737 sf at One Vanderbilt; adds 7,134 sf on 54th floor.
SL Green reports building 100% leased; asking rents $250–$300+/sf; term and rate undisclosed.
Tower 1.7M sf; trophy Midtown Manhattan location; strong institutional demand continues.
stories.summary: Private equity firm Sentinel Capital Partners expanded its footprint at SL Green's One Vanderbilt to 34,737 sf, adding 7,134 sf on the 54th floor. The building remains 100% leased with asking rents ranging from $250 to $300+/sf. The lease was negotiated by Newmark on behalf of Sentinel; SL Green used in-house brokers.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development; this is trophy office leasing in Manhattan. However, the continued 100% occupancy at One Vanderbilt at premium rents ($250–$300+/sf) indicates tight Class-A office supply in Midtown and sustained demand from financial/PE tenants. This does not signal office conversion urgency or rental apartment demand in the CBD; rather, it reinforces bifurcation between trophy Class-A (fully leased) and commodity/secondary office space (conversion candidates). Multifamily developers should focus conversion pipelines on lower-grade stock.

stories.title: Hedge Fund Castle Hook Takes Penthouse Office at Related’s 625 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: New York-based hedge fund manager Castle Hook Partners has landed the penthouse office lease at Related Companies’ upcoming 625 Madison Avenue tower. According to a memorandum of lease filed in city records Monday, Castle Hook inked a deal for the entire 52nd and 53rd floors of the planned 53-story development. The asking rent was not disclosed, but there’s no doubt that Castle Hook paid a premium. Related is seeking rents of up to $400 per square foot for the tower’s upper floors, the Wall Street Journal reported in July. The 15-year lease term includes options to renew an additional 10 years. Castle Hook currently lists its headquarters at BXP’s 767 Fifth Avenue, known as the General Motors Building. It is unknown whether the lease with Related represents a relocation or an expansion for the firm. A spokesperson for Related declined to comment on the deal, and the Castle Hook team did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Castle Hook’s deal follows global investment firm General Atlantic’s 152,000-square-foot commitment at 625 Madison Avenue, announced earlier this month. The future anchor tenant is slated to occupy five floors. Private equity firm Veritas Capital also appeared to secure 92,743 square feet at the development, according to Colliers’ August Manhattan office snapshot report. Ralph Lauren’s Polo Bar is also in talks to relocate to Related’s tower, according to WSJ, signaling the iconic restaurant’s potential relocation from 1 East 55th Street. Related’s Philippe Visser signed the mid-September deal on behalf of the developer. David Rogers, an executive officer at Castle Hook, signed for the tenant. It is unclear whether outside brokers were involved in the transaction. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Castle Hook Partners signs 52nd–53rd floor penthouse lease at Related's 625 Madison Avenue tower.
15-year term with 10-year renewal options; asking rents up to $400/sf for upper floors.
Hedge fund relocating from BXP's 767 Fifth Avenue (General Motors Building); deal status unclear.
stories.summary: Hedge fund Castle Hook Partners leased the entire 52nd and 53rd floor penthouse at Related's planned 53-story 625 Madison Avenue development on a 15-year term with 10-year renewal options. Related is seeking rents up to $400/sf on upper floors. Castle Hook is currently headquartered at the General Motors Building but the lease may represent relocation or expansion.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development. This is premium Manhattan office leasing at ultra-high rents ($400/sf), indicating persistent demand from financial services tenants for trophy space. Does not signal office conversion pressure; rather, it underscores that trophy Manhattan office remains supply-constrained and commands premium pricing. Multifamily developers should monitor only if Related's build timeline impacts nearby residential developments or capital markets sentiment.

stories.title: Elysee Investments Buys Shopping Center Near Waterford Business District for $28M
stories.excerpt: Elysee Investments paid $28 million for a relatively new, fully leased shopping center near Miami’s Waterford Business District. Called Blue Lagoon Shoppes, the 29,205-square-foot property at 1101 Northwest 57th Avenue sits inside the business district, just south of Miami International Airport. The 250-acre Waterford Business District is home to the headquarters of major companies such as Burger King, Subway and Lennar Homes. Blue Lagoon Shoppes’ 13 tenants include Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera Bread, Jersey Mike’s, BankUnited and Panda Express. Mario Borda of Borda Commercial Real Estate represented Elysee Investments, while Avison Young’s Michael T. Fay, John K. Crotty, David Duckworth and Brian C. de la Fé represented the seller, Keystone Holdings Group. “The strongest-performing retail investments today are the ones that combine essential-service tenancy with irreplaceable locations,” Avison Young’s de la Fé said in a statement. “Blue Lagoon Shoppes delivers both through its national-credit tenant roster, full occupancy and strong location.” Keystone Holdings Group completed the 2.4-acre asset in 2021. Elysee Investments specializes in retail properties in Miami-Dade and Broward counties. In 2024, the investor bought a 6.7-acre, grocery store-anchored property in Aventura for $48 million. Representatives for Elysee Investments and Keystone Holdings Group did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Update: The story was updated to include Michael T. Fay’s involvement. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Elysee Investments acquires Blue Lagoon Shoppes, 29,205 sf shopping center, Miami for $28M.
Property fully leased with 13 national tenants (Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera, BankUnited, Panda Express).
Located inside 250-acre Waterford Business District near Miami International Airport; home to Burger King, Subway, Lennar HQs.
stories.summary: Elysee Investments purchased Blue Lagoon Shoppes, a fully leased 29,205 sf shopping center near Miami's Waterford Business District, for $28 million. The property features 13 national-credit tenants including Starbucks, Chipotle, Panera, BankUnited, and Panda Express. The Waterford Business District is anchored by major corporate headquarters (Burger King, Subway, Lennar).
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. This is retail acquisition activity, not a demand or supply signal for apartments. However, the Waterford Business District's presence of major corporate HQs (Burger King, Subway, Lennar) and the robust retailer base indicate a stable, employer-dense submarket. Multifamily developers exploring Miami should note that Waterford offers potential workforce housing opportunities near job centers; the influx of essential-service retail suggests demographic stability. Monitor this area for future multifamily infill near corporate campuses.

stories.title: Brixmor Property Group, Everview Partners Acquire Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34B
stories.excerpt: One of the largest owners of shopping centers in the U.S. just got bigger. Brixmor Property Group, a $9 billion publicly traded real estate investment trust (REIT) and holder of a portfolio of 346 shopping centers spanning more than 63 million square feet, announced Monday that it has partnered with Everview Partners to acquire Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34 billion. Slate Grocery REIT has a portfolio of 115 grocery-anchored, open-air retail centers that together comprise 15.7 million square feet of real estate. Under the terms of the deal, Brixmor will acquire 23 shopping centers in Florida, Georgia and the two Carolinas for $636 million, but will form an institutional joint venture with Everview Partners and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority that will acquire the remaining 92 assets from Slate Grocery REIT for $1.71 billion. Brian Finnegan, Brixmor’s CEO and president, told Commercial Observer on Monday that his firm was motivated to finalize the deal with Everview Partners after seeing a large amount of institutional capital enter the open-air, grocery-anchored retail space in recent years and “validate the asset class.” “This opportunity to get 23 assets that we’re purchasing ourselves, as part of a broader portfolio where we can leverage the platform, just made a lot of sense to bring in a partner like Everview,” he said. “[The new portfolio] is in markets we know really well with a lot of growth potential, redevelopment opportunities right out the gate, and significant mark-to-market rent opportunities, as well. Brixmor plans to grow “long-standing grocer relationships” and capitalize on numerous “remerchandising, redevelopment, and outparcel opportunities,” according to a release. bullets: Brixmor Property Group and Everview Partners acquire Slate Grocery REIT for $2.34B; 115 properties, 15.7M sf.
Brixmor acquires 23 centers in FL, GA, Carolinas for $636M; JV with Everview/Abu Dhabi Authority for 92 remaining.
Deal driven by institutional capital flow into grocery-anchored, open-air retail; Brixmor now 346+ centers, 63M+ sf.
stories.summary: Brixmor Property Group and Everview Partners announced a $2.34 billion acquisition of Slate Grocery REIT, comprising 115 grocery-anchored shopping centers totaling 15.7 million sf. Brixmor will directly acquire 23 centers in Florida, Georgia, and the Carolinas for $636 million, while forming an institutional joint venture with Everview Partners and the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority for the remaining 92 assets. The deal reflects strong institutional capital flow into open-air grocery-anchored retail.
stories.impact: Minimal direct relevance to multifamily development; this is pure retail/shopping center consolidation. However, the deal signals that institutional capital (Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth, PE firms) views grocery-anchored retail as recession-resilient and counter-cyclical. This capital deployment trend could compete with multifamily for institutional equity and debt in secondary markets (Southeast focus). Multifamily developers should monitor: (1) whether Brixmor/Everview pursue mixed-use or adaptive-use opportunities at underperforming centers (potential conversion upside for apartments), and (2) whether capital flows to grocery-anchored retail reduce debt availability for MF development in the Southeast.
